title: Miami Spice Back with New Reserve Tier and 300 Restaurants
summary: The 25th edition of Miami Spice Restaurant Months is back from August 1 through September 30, 2026. This year’s program from The Greater Miami Convention & Visitors Bureau (GMCVB) features three-course prix-fixe menus at a minimum of 30% savings at more than 300 participating…
whatHappening: Miami Spice Restaurant Month is returning for its 25th year, running August 1 through September 30, 2026. The program now features a new reserve tier and includes over 300 participating restaurants offering three-course prix-fixe menus at minimum 30% savings.
whoInvolved: The Greater Miami Convention & Visitors Bureau (GMCVB) is organizing the program, a destination marketing organization that promotes Miami as a travel and convention destination. The initiative brings together hundreds of independent and chain restaurants across the Miami area.
whyMatters: The expanded program with 300+ restaurants and a new reserve tier signals growing participation and sophistication in Miami's dining promotion efforts, potentially boosting tourism during the late summer and early fall period. articleBody:
Miami's celebrated restaurant promotion returns this August with expanded offerings and a fresh tier structure. The 25th edition of Miami Spice Restaurant Month, according to Miami Curated, will run from August 1 through September 30, 2026, featuring participation from more than 300 restaurants across the greater Miami area. The program, organized by The Greater Miami Convention & Visitors Bureau, is introducing a new reserve tier this year alongside its traditional prix-fixe offerings, allowing diners to access three-course menus at a minimum of 30% savings.

The introduction of a reserve tier represents a strategic expansion of the program's scope. By creating a tiered structure, organizers can accommodate both casual dining establishments and upscale restaurants, broadening the appeal to different diner preferences and budgets. The reserve tier likely targets food enthusiasts and special-occasion diners seeking elevated experiences, while the standard program maintains accessibility for everyday diners seeking value.

Miami Spice has become a marquee event on the culinary calendar, drawing both locals and visitors eager to explore the region's diverse restaurant scene at reduced prices. The summer and early fall timing capitalizes on the transition between seasonal tourism patterns, helping restaurants maintain steady traffic during months that might otherwise see slower business. By anchoring the program to a two-month window, the GMCVB creates sustained promotional momentum rather than a one-time spike.

The participation of over 300 restaurants underscores the program's reach and importance to Miami's dining economy. This substantial number suggests successful outreach to establishments across various neighborhoods, cuisines, and price points. For participating restaurants, the guaranteed promotional visibility and increased customer volume justify the discounted pricing structure, creating a mutually beneficial arrangement that strengthens the overall dining destination brand.

The guaranteed 30% minimum savings on prix-fixe menus represents a meaningful incentive for consumers. Rather than open-ended discounts that vary by establishment, the standardized savings structure simplifies decision-making for diners and ensures consistency in value across the program. This clarity has likely contributed to Miami Spice's longevity and reputation as a reliable opportunity for culinary exploration.

title: Where Elegance Lives: 5 Wonderful Miami Bars
summary: One of my go-to spots when I’m in New York City is the iconic King Cole Bar at the St. Regis. Stepping inside always feels like an immersion into a bygone era—a time when elegance was a deeply desired way of life. Even as modern fashion has shifted toward the casual, the bar…
whatHappening: Miami Curated has published a feature highlighting five elegant bars in Miami, drawing inspiration from classic cocktail culture and sophisticated atmospheres. The piece opens with a reflection on the iconic King Cole Bar at the St. Regis in New York City, using that benchmark of refinement to frame Miami's own upscale drinking establishments.
whoInvolved: Miami Curated, a lifestyle publication focused on the Miami area, is the publisher. The King Cole Bar at the St. Regis New York—a legendary luxury venue housed in a 1904 hotel designed by Trowbridge & Livingston and now operated by Marriott International—serves as the article's point of reference for classical elegance.
whyMatters: The piece reflects an ongoing cultural conversation about maintaining formal elegance and sophistication amid shifting fashion and social norms toward casualness. For Miami's hospitality and tourism sectors, visibility in curated lifestyle guides drives foot traffic to upscale venues and reinforces the city's positioning as a destination for refined dining and cocktail experiences.
articleBody:
The St. Regis New York's King Cole Bar has long stood as a temple of old-world glamour in Manhattan's Midtown neighborhood. Located at the luxury hotel originally developed by John Jacob Astor IV and completed in 1904, the bar evokes an era when elegance was not merely aspirational but a deeply ingrained way of life. The hotel itself, now operated by Marriott International and holding both Forbes five-star and AAA five-diamond ratings, has maintained this standard for over a century.

It is precisely this model of timeless sophistication that Miami Curated uses as a touchstone in its feature exploring five wonderful bars across Miami. According to Miami Curated, stepping into venues like the King Cole Bar feels like an immersion into a bygone era—a quality the publication suggests Miami's finest establishments have successfully cultivated. Even as contemporary fashion and social behavior have shifted decisively toward the casual, these bars maintain an aesthetic and atmosphere rooted in a more formal tradition.

The contrast between nostalgia and modernity lies at the heart of the feature's appeal. The King Cole Bar was designed during the Beaux-Arts period and has remained largely unchanged in character, despite the hotel's expansions—an annex was added in 1927 by architects Sloan & Robertson. This commitment to preserving elegance across decades offers a lesson for Miami's bar scene, where establishing a sense of timelessness requires both intentional design and unwavering standards of service.

Miami's emergence as a destination for sophisticated cocktail culture reflects broader trends in hospitality, where travelers increasingly seek experiences that feel removed from the everyday. The five bars highlighted in the feature represent venues that have chosen to resist the pull toward informality, instead doubling down on the trappings and rituals of elegant drinking—careful bartending, refined interiors, and an atmosphere of understated luxury.

For Miami's hospitality industry, such curated features serve an important function in shaping perceptions of the city's lifestyle offerings. By drawing an explicit line between Miami establishments and iconic venues like the King Cole Bar, the publication positions local bars as worthy successors to a longer tradition of refined American cocktail culture. This positioning helps attract visitors and residents who prioritize elegance and are willing to support venues that maintain exacting standards.
